playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: start near center (cells 3–7) and then move to an unused cell each subsequent round to avoid being trivially guessed. If an opponent repeatedly fires the same cell at me or scores on it, move away from that cell immediately; if an opponent repeatedly misses on the same cell and it is safe strategically, consider hiding there once to bait them—only do this when I judge the risk acceptable.

When I see others’ shot cells and results, track patterns across rounds. If someone repeatedly fires the same cell and scores, assume that cell is currently occupied and avoid it. If someone fires the same cell repeatedly and keeps missing, mark that cell as a potential bait and consider probing it only when I can profit. Use successes I observe (my own hits or others’ public hit claims) as strong evidence of a hide and use that to choose my shots or hides accordingly.

When posting a station note, keep it short, neutral, and actionable: use "steady on station" or explicitly propose an escort arrangement naming one specific boat if I intend to try to set up a reciprocal escort. If I propose an escort in a note, follow up by naming that boat in my salvage claim the same round I expect reciprocity; do not rely on vague or late proposals.

When the standing order directs a target, follow it unless there is a clear tactical reason to deviate (e.g., target is Harbor and jettison risk is unacceptable, or I have strong evidence another live station is on a high-probability cell I can exploit). If I deviate, pick the live boat most likely to be on the cell I choose based on observed hits/misses and claimed shots.

When choosing a firing cell, use all available evidence: prefer cells that have been shown to hold the target recently, prefer central cells early in the patrol for coverage, but do not repeat the exact same probe every round without reason—vary probes to avoid being predictable. If I have no information, use probing shots distributed across the line rather than repeatedly firing the same cell; if I have observed a successful hit pattern against a boat, attack that cell to score.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report it truthfully ([claim: hit] or [claim: miss]) because the public claim must match the private result and truthful reporting keeps my public information consistent and useful for future inferences.

When making an escort claim, only claim to have escorted a boat if I have clear reciprocal intent or evidence (e.g., I wrote a note proposing an escort and the other responded or named me back that same round). To secure mutual escorts, propose explicitly in the note then name the same partner in salvage on the next round only if they indicated reciprocity; if no reciprocity is shown, claim none. If I can coordinate simultaneous mutual naming (both name each other in salvage), take it—5 points each is worth arranging.

Never fire at Harbor unless the expected gain (3 points transferred plus potential tactical advantage) clearly outweighs the guaranteed political/social cost and risk of coordinated retaliation; only take Harbor’s payroll if I can reasonably avoid being put off the board by coordinated retaliation or if I can accept the consequences.

When others repeat successful patterns (e.g., firing the same cell and getting hits), assume they are targeting a stationary hide and act to either exploit that knowledge (fire at that cell) when they are the target or avoid being in that hide if they might target me. When my own shots reveal a boat’s hide (I score hits), exploit that info in subsequent rounds or share neutral notes to encourage reciprocity when advantageous.

When my shots repeatedly miss against the same opponent, reassess whether they are changing hides unpredictably; switch to probing shots across different cells to learn their pattern rather than continuing low-probability guesses. Use misses to eliminate cells systematically.

When I can coordinate points via notes and escort promises, be proactive: propose a specific partner early enough that they can reciprocate that round, and if they do not reciprocate, do not invent claims later. If I finish a round with no clear reciprocity or evidence of escorting, claim none rather than inventing escorts.

Be mindful of my firing and hiding symmetry: avoid always firing or hiding in the same cells (I used 5 repeatedly in the playthrough and scored hits because the target happened to be there, but repeating that pattern is predictable). Vary firing cells unless I have confirmed that a target remains on a particular cell and I want to exploit it.

Follow standing order by default (Echo→Foxtrot→Gamma→Echo). If I repeatedly score under the standing order, continue; if the standing order would force me into a poor tactical choice (e.g., firing Harbor under high risk), override it with a justified alternative and be prepared to explain it via neutral notes.

When proposing escorts, expect that a simple proposal in the note without explicit salvage naming may not be enough; plan to name the partner in salvage the same round reciprocity is indicated. If I propose and the other names me back, claim the escort to collect the payoff. If no one agrees, prioritize scoring via shots over chasing unlikely escorts.

Keep all public statements consistent with private results and with the factual constraints (coordinate validation, claim matching private shot result). Use public truthfulness as a tool to build reliable inferences from others’ statements.

After each patrol, revise hiding and firing heuristics based on observed opponent behavior: if an opponent is predictable, exploit it; if they adapt, increase probing variety.

1.text:
When asked to hide, randomize within a controlled band and avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row; prefer midboard (4–6) when I have no info, but alternate edges (2–3, 7–8) regularly to break predictability and avoid being trailed by sequential shooters. Do not lock on a single cell for multiple consecutive rounds.

When notes are requested, post short, specific signals that can be interpreted as commitments (e.g., “will escort X”, “escort me Echo?”, or “holding station”) so I can coordinate reciprocal escorts; don’t post useless fluff. If I propose a mutual escort, I will look for an explicit reciprocation from the other boat before committing my salvage. Treat “steady on station” as weak/no-commitment intelligence.

When proposing an escort in my note, phrase it to require confirmation (e.g., “will escort Echo if Echo escorts me” or “escort Echo? reciprocate?”). If I receive a clear reciprocal pledge in a later note from the intended partner in the same round, follow through with the salvage claim; otherwise name none.

When the standing order tells me whom to fire on, follow it unless that target is Harbor or shooting them would create a clear tactical disadvantage (e.g., coordinated retaliation risk, guaranteed jettison penalty without compensation). If the standing order targets Harbor, do not shoot Harbor unless I have explicit coordination and accept the jettison consequence.

When I must choose a fired cell with no intel, bias toward center cells for coverage (4–6), but explicitly vary across rounds (rotate among 4,5,6 and occasionally 3 or 7) so I am not predictable to opponents who can observe my history. Do not fire the same cell in three consecutive rounds.

When I have private confirmation of a hit, always claim hit publicly; when I have private confirmation of a miss, always claim miss publicly — do not falsify claims. Accurate claims preserve credibility needed for mutual escort trades.

When I can arrange mutual escort claims, do so (name each other) to secure easy +5 points each round; use notes to propose and confirm these exchanges and only execute when reciprocated. When I can’t arrange a mutual escort, name none rather than wasting it on a nonreciprocal or low-value target.

When behind on points and an opportunity exists to legally reduce a leader’s score with a shot (and without unreasonable retaliation), prioritize that target while balancing risk. Conversely, when ahead on points, play more conservatively: avoid risky plays that would provoke coordinated retaliation or target Harbor unnecessarily.

When opponents (or a specific boat) show a pattern of firing at me, break pattern by changing hide choices and publicly signaling a defensive posture to discourage further focus (e.g., “holding edges this round”). If being targeted repeatedly, deprioritize escort offers until I can reestablish trust.

When coordinating with teammates via notes, use unambiguous short phrases and follow through; failing to follow through loses credibility and ruins future negotiated mutual escorts. If I pledge an escort publicly, only abandon it with a short truthful note explaining why (e.g., “no reciprocation last round — no escort”).

Do not assume others’ notes reflect binding commitments — verify reciprocation or see a pattern of follow-through over multiple rounds before trusting them for repeated mutual escorts. Echoing “steady on station” or similar vague signals is insufficient basis for committing salvage.

Avoid attacking Harbor unless explicit side-benefit or negotiated compensation is available; uncoordinated attacks on Harbor produce certain penalties and often result in net loss.

If I see successful reciprocal escort trades happening between two other boats repeatedly, consider whether disrupting them (by targeting one legally) yields a better expected return than attempting to join them; choose disruption only when I can expect a net point gain after retaliation risk.

When tempted to be unpredictable for its own sake (e.g., random words, meaningless notes), don’t — every public message should serve a tactical purpose I can act on next round.

Maintain a private logging habit: track which boats reciprocate escorts, which return fire on my hides, and which hide cells they tend to use; use that log to inform hide variation, target selection, and trust decisions next game.

2.text:
When asked for a hide, randomize within a small biased set: if I am being targeted successfully by another boat, pick an edge/corner (choose from 1,3,7,9) to shift my pattern; otherwise pick a midboard cell (rotate among 4,5,6). Never repeat the exact same hide three rounds in a row. If forced to change twice in a row, switch sets (mid -> edge or edge -> mid). Always send a valid integer 1–9.

When posting a station note, use it to coordinate a future mutual escort: explicitly propose a partner by name and an explicit round (e.g., "propose escort with X next round"). Do not post empty boilerplate every round. If another boat publicly proposes an escort naming me for an upcoming round, reply either by (a) publicly proposing them back for that round, or (b) if that round is the current round and I can file salvage now, be prepared to file the reciprocal salvage. Do not claim escort without a prior public proposal from me or clear reciprocal public proposal from the partner.

When firing, follow any standing order about target identity. Vary aim based on past information: if I have a recent private hit on a target, bias my next shot at that target toward the hit cell for one round only; otherwise choose from the small plausible set for that target (prefer central set 4,5,6 early game, expand to edges if I suspect avoidance). If an opponent has repeatedly hit my hides, change my hide pattern (edge/corner rotation) rather than keep shooting the same cell. If my previous shot at the same target was a miss, do not repeat the identical firing coordinate two rounds running unless I have reason to believe the target stayed there.

Never fire at Harbor unless executing a deliberate, sacrifice-forced strategy that accepts the guaranteed penalty; assume attacking Harbor is normally negative EV and avoid it.

When I receive the private result of my shot, always file the claim equal to that true result. Do not lie in claims. Filing truth preserves credibility and helps coordinate escorts.

When naming an escort (salvage), only name an actual live boat and only do so when I have either: (a) already publicly proposed a mutual escort and received their public acceptance for that round, or (b) the other boat has publicly proposed me for that round and I will reciprocate that same round. If no mutual arrangement is in place, file salvage: none. Do not name a boat that was not publicly proposed or is already sunk/removed.

When I want the mutual-escort 5-point payoff, set it up openly: in my note propose the partner and the explicit round; if they agree in their note, on the agreed round both file each other as escorts. If the partner does not agree publicly before the escort stage, do not unilaterally claim escort. If a partner publicly proposes me and I accept, be ready to file the salvage that same round even if I was also hit or otherwise distracted.

If I am repeatedly being hit by one particular opponent, prioritize changing hide behavior immediately and prioritize targeting that opponent when it is my standing-order target so I can deter them; do not persist with a fixed cell that has been hit before. If I have reliable evidence of the cell they used to hit me, consider aiming at that cell when I get to fire at them.

If my shot history produces a hit, keep using information from that hit (the cell) to predict their future hide shifts for one round only, then revert to randomized rotation among the plausible set. Do not overfit to a single earlier hit beyond one follow-up.

Avoid obvious predictable patterns: alternate between posting a coordination note and brief neutral notes rather than always posting identical text; rotate firing coordinates and hide locations within the chosen sets; do not always fire the same coordinate (e.g., always 5).

When balancing between a single-shot hit (4 points) versus securing a mutual escort payoff (5 points each), prefer the escort if I can reliably set it up with a public proposal and observable reciprocation; otherwise pursue hits on the most vulnerable live opponent according to standing orders and hit evidence.

Ensure all inputs are valid: hides are integers 1–9; fire coordinates are integers 1–9; targets and salvage names are live boat names only; claims are either hit or miss.

Maintain honesty in claims and escorts to preserve future coordination options. If trust breaks down (partners ignore proposals or repeatedly defect), revert to targeting for hits and defensive hiding rather than further earnest proposals.

Operational details I will act on:
- Hide rotation pools: mid-pool {4,5,6}; edge/corner pool {1,3,7,9}; occasional gapped offsets {2,8} if needed to avoid repetition.
- Do not repeat any exact hide coordinate three times consecutively.
- If I score a hit on a target at cell X, next time I fire at that target bias to X; if miss, pick next from the same pool but not X if X just missed.
- If another boat publicly proposes me for an escort this round, reciprocate in salvage immediately; if they propose me for a future round, publicly accept by proposing them back for that same round so intentions are synchronous.
- Do not file salvage: <boat> unless there is a clear public proposal-exchange consistent with mutual intent.
